images.caption: This is a bust of Adolphus Busch (1839-1913) in the Bauernhof at Grant's Farm near Affton Missouri, USA. German-born Busch co-founded Anheuser-Busch brewery. The sculptor, Johannes Boese (1856-1917) did several sculptures of Busch and his family in the latter part of his career.

images.filename: August A Busch Castle in Grantwood Village MO.png
images.caption: German-American brewer August Anheuser Busch Sr. acquired a large fraction of the old Ulysses S. Grant tract in Affton, Missouri (now Grantwood Village, Missouri) in 1903 and built a palatial house in its midst in 1910. Designed by the firm Widmann & Walsh, it still stands today.
images.alt: German-American brewer August Anheuser Busch Sr. acquired a large fraction of the old Ulysses S. Grant tract in Affton, Missouri (now Grantwood Village, Missouri) in 1903 and built a palatial house in its midst in 1910. Designed by the firm Widmann & Walsh, it still stands today.

images.caption: German-American brewer August Anheuser Busch Sr. acquired a large fraction of the old Ulysses S. Grant tract in Affton, Missouri (now Grantwood Village, Missouri) in 1903 and in 1914 built The Bauernhof in its midst. Designed by the firm Klipstein & Rathman, this photo shows the north end of the great hall with view into the next chamber where horses are bathed. Clearly visible is the significant use that was made of Hy-tex "Hy-namel" white and green glazed enamel brick from the Hydraulic-Press Brick Company of St. Louis.

images.filename: Bust of Otto von Bismarck - Close-up.jpg
images.caption: This is a bust of Otto von Bismarck (1815-1898) in the Bauernhof at Grant's Farm near Affton Missouri, USA. The sculptor, Reinhold Begas (1831-1911) did this particular bust in 1886. Inscription reads Fuerst Bismarck Kanzler des deutschen Reiches, which translates as "Prince Bismarck, Chancellor of the German Empire".
images.alt: This is a bust of Otto von Bismarck (1815-1898) in the Bauernhof at Grant's Farm near Affton Missouri, USA. The sculptor, Reinhold Begas (1831-1911) did this particular bust in 1886.
